/w/.git/hooks/commit-msg is installed and active (its source is also at /w/tools/commit-msg). It enforces this team's message convention and prints the rule it rejected on. Satisfy it: do NOT edit, delete, replace or bypass it, and never pass `--no-verify`. Discover its rules by running it or by reading it.

TASK A - fix the parser. /w/src/csv.js exports `parseCsvLine(record)`, which must turn one CSV record into an array of fields:
  - fields are separated by commas; `parseCsvLine("")` is the empty array `[]`, while `parseCsvLine(",")` is `["", ""]`;
  - a field may be wrapped in double quotes; inside quotes a doubled `""` means one literal quote, and commas are literal text;
  - surrounding whitespace is never trimmed, and unquoted fields are taken literally;
  - a closing quote must be followed by a comma or the end of the record, otherwise throw `new Error("text after closing quote")`;
  - a quoted field that never closes throws `new Error("unterminated quote")`.
  `node tests/run_parser_tests.js` prints `PARSER OK` when it is right. Do not modify anything under /w/tests/ or /w/data/.

TASK B - drop the legacy splitter. Delete /w/src/legacy_split.js from the repository and from disk, and stop /w/src/index.js from importing it, keeping `parseCsvLine` exported exactly as it is now. No file under /w/src, /w/tools or /w/tests may still mention `legacy_split` afterwards. /w/tools/report.js must keep working unmodified: `node tools/report.js` must print exactly
  rows=5 total=1284 top=Line, with, commas

TASK C - commit that work as exactly TWO commits on `main`, in this order:
  1. subject line exactly `fix(csv): parse quoted fields`, containing ONLY src/csv.js;
  2. subject line exactly `refactor(csv): drop the legacy splitter`, containing ONLY src/index.js and the deletion of src/legacy_split.js.
  The last line of BOTH messages must be exactly `Ref: TICKET-4417`. Everything else about the message shape is the commit-msg hook's business.

TASK D - write /w/.git/hooks/pre-commit, executable, that blocks a commit when any STAGED file whose path ends in `.js` contains a tab character or a line longer than 100 characters. It must judge the staged content (what `git show :<path>` or `git diff --cached` reports), NOT the working-tree copy, so that a commit still succeeds when only the unstaged copy offends. For each offending line it prints exactly one line
  PRECOMMIT <path>:<lineno>: <reason>
where <path> is the repository-relative path exactly as git reports it (a staged path may contain spaces), <lineno> is 1-based, and <reason> is `tab` or `long-line`, and then it exits non-zero. A line that is both long and contains a tab prints both, tab first. When nothing offends, it prints nothing and exits 0. It must ignore deleted paths and files that are not `.js`. This hook also applies to your own commits above, so keep your JavaScript free of tabs and under 101 columns.
